title: Convoy TAMA-17, 29–30 April 1944
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · Coordinated attack group, Capt. G. E. Peterson

participants.name: PARCHE
participants.co: LCdr L. P. Ramage; pack commander Capt. G. E. Peterson aboard

paras.text: BANG's first attacks: four approaches on convoy TAMA-17 west of Luzon over the night of 29–30 April, with PARCHE and TINOSA closing in on her reports. Every mark is a position or attack typed into the boats' war patrol reports, beside the Japanese record of the same minutes, on one GMT clock.
Japanese loss list: Takegawa Maru (1,930 GRT) and Nittatsu Maru (2,859 GRT), both to BANG. No loss matches PARCHE's or TINOSA's attacks next morning; the rest reached Manila on 2 May.
Takao to Manila, sailed 1300 on 28 April. Its ships, as the escort division's table, Nittatsu Maru's movement log and combinedfleet.com name them, are in the convoy's own record: [[convoy:tama-17]].

Positions are the boats' own dead reckoning and star sights, and three navigators never quite agree, so the same convoy appears in slightly different places in each report. Lines between positions are straight; where a boat actually went in between is not recorded. Dashed outlines mark entries the report itself contradicts, kept with the reason.

BANG kept zone K (−10) and PARCHE zone I (−9); TINOSA kept zone H (−8) on station. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). On 29–30 April the target ship's own log and BANG's attack sheets agree to within one to seven minutes once both are in GMT.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (BANG 74802746, PARCHE 74828582, TINOSA 74856363). Nittatsu Maru's movement log and the 1st Surface Escort Division war diary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy lists from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

paras.text: Takao to Manila, sailed 1300 on 28 April 1944 (the escort division's table). Only one ship's cargo is recorded: Nittatsu Maru loaded 250 t of coal at Takao to be landed at Manila (her master's log, p23). The other ships' cargoes and the convoy's arrival are not in the records read. BANG attacked it on 29–30 April; PARCHE and TINOSA were in the same action (the engagement of 29–30 April, which says which boat attacked which).

Lists of the convoy drawn from combinedfleet.com give thirteen merchant ships. Eleven are on combinedfleet's page for Nittatsu Maru (28 April: Kennichi, Kurogane, Belgium, Peking, Shiroganesan, Takegawa, Tsushima, San Luis, Wales, Yamahagi and Shirotae Maru, escorted by Harukaze, W-17 and the auxiliary gunboat Chohakusan Maru; Asakaze joined on the 29th). Takegawa Maru is also in the Japanese record; the other ten are listed here as secondary. Nissan Maru, and the Yashima and Hakka Maru that "other lists add", are on no page found, so they are left out. combinedfleet's Chohakusan Maru is the escort division table's Chojusan Maru (as read).

words.type_attack: Night periscope depth attack. Fired four torpedoes using 1° spread between torpedoes applied from forward aft by means of the offset knob on TDC, at DD range 1800 yards in line with AK range 3000 yards and second AK range 4000 yards; then fired two torpedoes using 2° spread from forward aft by means of offset knob on TDC at AO range 2800 yards.
words.description: Convoy consisting of at least 12 ships with minimum of 4 DD escorts (Probably 8 or more escorts). One AO, one AP and four fleet type destroyers identified. Others seemed to be 5000-9000 ton AK's. Contact initially made by sighting smoke through periscope while submerged. Bright moonlit night at time of attack.
words.damaged: One 7000 ton AK probably sunk. One 8000 ton AO damaged. One AK or DD possibly damaged.
words.determined_by: Saw torpedo hit AK followed by smoke from her bow to bridge. Heard torpedo explosion at time of this hit. Heard high noise level and popping noises at 400 feet over JK ten minutes after attack on bearing of the AK, which may have been her sinking. Heard two other torpedo explosions one timed to hit AO, the other possibly a second hit in first AK or a hit in another AK or DD.

words.remarks: Below Sketch shows conditions as seen at time of firing. Torpedoes hit at 02m 10s; 02m 12s; and 02m 39s. after firing. From the below table it can be seen that there are various combinations of possible hits. The only hit observed corresponded to the time of the first explosion and was in AK1. It is believed that the first two hits were in this AK and that the discrepancy between the difference between the time of explosions, 2 seconds, and between time of firing, 8 seconds, is due to different running speeds of the two torpedoes; and that the third hit was in the AO. ... Only one degree spread between torpedoes was used when firing at the DD to enhance the poasibility of hits on the Marus in line with her.
words.note: Two targets on one sheet. Tubes 1-4 (FIRST TARGET) were fired on the TDC solution for the DD at 1800 yards, in line with an AK at 3000 and a second AK at 4000 (type attack; remarks, p18), so attacks.csv gives the DD's draft and range for them; the one hit seen was in AK1, not the DD. Tubes 5 and 6 (SECOND TARGET) are the AO's. The type attack says the AO pair was fired with a 2° spread; the table types 1R and 1L, which is 2° between them. The remarks continue on p18 with a table of torpedo runs against the times of the three hits (#2 at 2-10, #3 at 2-12, #6 at 2-39 underlined, matching the table's Hit column) and a sketch of the convoy. The sheet's damage lines say none sunk and one AK probably sunk.

words.type_attack: Night surface radar attack, using constant radar ranges and constant TBT bearings to TDC. Used 1° spread between torpedoes, applied from forward aft by means of the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: One large AP of convoy of attack No. 1. This ship was at first believed to be a 17000 ton AP, but later identification with large angle on the bow at range of 1300 yards showed her silhouette to be identical to that of page 88 of O.N.I. 208-J (issue August 24, 1942), a 10400 ton AP. One DD escort patrolling ahead; two other DD's that had been patrolling astern had just left her.

words.remarks: Target zigged right immediately after firing. Spread was offset one degree to right realizing that a zig to the right would give the target the greatest chance to avoid. If the spread had been applied from aft forward I do not believe the target could have avoided since the first torpedo reached the track 40 seconds before the last one did.

words.note: The gyro is typed *195 for all four stern tubes, the asterisk pointing to the remarks: the TDC's after angle solver was not solving and the gyro should have been 184. attacks.csv keeps 195 as typed. From own course 340 and target course 180, gyro 195 gives a track of 175S, against the typed 160S (check_attacks.py: DISAGREES, 15°); the corrected 184 would give 164S. The typed track, own course, target course and gyro were re-read at zoom (p21, p22) and are as typed: the disagreement is the sheet's own, the fault its remarks describe. All four missed.

Fired the fourth torpedo with torpedo gyro set on zero using lead angle from bridge.

words.own_ship: Speed: 4 knots Course: 320°T. Depth: Surface Angle: 0° (at firing)
words.remarks: I checked fire after the third torpedo left the tube because the first two torpedo wakes seemed to be leading the target too much (This impression was natural because the first two torpedoes were spread ahead of the MOT), and having seen 10 previous torpedoes miss this target I decided to fire the fourth torpedo bow and arrow; so came right, took a 10° lead on the stern and fired with a zero gyro angle. I knew that a zig toward could not make this torpedo miss, whereas I thought a zig away would bring the other torpedoes on better. The second and third torpedoes hit at 1m 15s, and 1m 23s after firing - there was very little left of the target when the fourth torpedo got there.
words.note: One track angle, 60S, is typed for all four. The fourth torpedo (tube 2, gyro 000) was fired 1-05 (65 seconds) after the first, after the boat "came right"; the sheet gives only the one own course, 320, so its computed track (50S) is 10° off the typed 60S. Tube 3 (gyro 015) computes to 65S. Kept as typed. The typed spread of the first three (4½R, 1½R, 1½L) steps 3°, as the type attack says. The table's hits (tubes 4 and 1) match the remarks' second and third torpedoes.

words.type_attack: Submerged periscope attack from ahead. Made end around and dived ahead of convoy with tops in sight. Convoy consisted of ten ships disposed in three columns in line, zig-zagging 40° right and left of the base course 200 T. The slick sea, bright sun, and two planes patrolling ahead necessitated going to 90 feet between periscope exposures. At 3000 yards we were 20° on port bow of center column, then maneuvered to gain position between center and port columns in order to fire both bow and stern tubes. At 1007 observed convoy had zigged radically to the left putting us 40 degrees on starboard bow of starboard column with no alternative but stern shots. 1010-11 Fired four MK 18 torpedoes from stern tubes; two each at first and second AK in starboard column. Just at firing the targets were observed to hoist a two pennant signal and commence turning away, having apparently seen the periscope slick. At 1013 observed no hits on targets but their maneuver put entire convoy on course about normal to torpedo tracks with all three columns overlapping. Was forced to go deep by aircraft but set up still looked good as all four torpedoes (electric) were heard running straight and normal in direction of convoy. At 1014 heard heavy explosion 3 min. 55 sec. after firing last torpedo which was believed to be a hit. 1018 Received first stick of aircraft bombs.

words.note: Every typed track is about 20° wider than own course + gyro + 180 - target course gives (91S typed, 69.5S computed for tube 7; the same for all four). Read twice on the scan: kept as typed. The sheet's target course (170 T) is the one solution for both ships; the narrative on the sheet has the targets turning away just at firing, which may be why. Range and draft per torpedo are inferred: the sheet types (1) 1750 yds, 18' and (2) 2250, 15', and says two torpedoes each at the first and second AK; tubes 7 and 8 (the first pair by firing interval and spread 1 R, 1 L) are given target (1), tubes 9 and 10 target (2). Firing intervals are typed 0, 11, 32, 55 sec.: they read as times from the first torpedo, not between torpedoes. All four typed Miss, with "One probable hit on another target" under the row.

words.narrative: 0919 (H) commenced firing all six bow tubes on 90° starboard track with a 3,000 yard torpedo run. Four hits were felt and heard which appeared to be the first, third, fourth and fifth torpedoes fired, hitting ships one, three and four. ... Number three tube was fired last with 0 spread, the second and last apparently straddling number two target.
words.basis: hit (Hit on the first, third, fourth and fifth rows; Miss on the second and sixth) and tube 3 on the sixth row from the narrative, rg38-74856363/p10; the rest from the summary table, p26.
words.note: A summary table, not a data sheet. Three drafts are typed for three targets (one AO, two AK) and one range (3,000), so the drafts are left out of attacks.csv: the narrative aims at the middle of a group of five overlapping ships, not at one. The narrative's hits are its own hedged reading ("appeared to be"); the misses are the two it says "apparently" straddled number two target. Its track (90° starboard) and run (3,000 yards) agree with the table. It fires at 0919 H (0119 GCT), 18 minutes before this table's 0137; the table's longitude is 63 nm east of the narrative's sinking position (positions.csv). The narrative gives no other tube numbers, and no own course, speed or depth at firing (at 0828 H she "came to course 070° to close the range", p09; not used as the firing course).
